payload.alt: Displacements a, b, and d point left, while c points right. Their sum is the total leftward displacement from d0 to df.
Painted portrait of Galileo with short hair and a reddish beard, wearing a black doublet with a white collar.
Mars Climate Orbiter above Mars, with a gold-covered body, three-panel solar array, and dish antenna.
Line graph of position (m) versus time (s): position rises from about 200 m at 0 s to 2,900 m at 30 s, with increasing slope.
Line graph of position (m) versus time (s): position rises linearly from about 2.5 m at 0 s to 19 m at 70 s.
Route diagram: home and school are 5 km apart. Opposite arrows show a round trip; initial and final positions coincide at home.
Displacement vectors: 3 km west followed by 2 km east puts the final position 1 km west of the start. East is positive; west is negative.
Graph of y versus x: the line rises with positive slope m, equal to rise divided by run, and crosses the y-axis at b above zero.
Line graph of position (m) versus time (s): rises from about 200 m to 2,900 m over 30 s, with a steeper tangent at Q than P.
A car on a winding road connects Home at the lower left with Friend’s house at the upper right.
A long, low jet-powered car points right on a paved track, with a large cloud of exhaust trailing behind it to the left.
Line graph of position (m) versus time (s): position rises linearly from 400 m; slope is average velocity, delta d divided by delta t.
Line graph of position (km) versus time (min): position rises steadily from 0 km at 0 minutes to 5 km at 10 minutes.
A car travels from home at initial position d zero to school at final position d f. An arrow points from home toward school.
A passenger jet seen from below against a blue sky with scattered clouds, with no ground or fixed landmarks visible.
Home and store are 3 km apart. Opposite arrows show the outward and return trips along the same path.
